title: Siri 18 Months Late: Apple Lands in Regulatory Crosshairs in South Korea Over Misleading iPhone 16 Ads

content_html:
When selling phones, Apple put features that “weren’t ready yet” into its ads—and once again ran into regulators. South Korea’s Fair Trade Commission has recently formally reviewed Apple, accusing it of misleading consumers in iPhone 16 ads: the visuals made people think features such as Genmoji, Image Playground, and Siri’s ability to understand personal context and on-screen content were already available, when some had in fact not been delivered.

One feature, 18 months late

The dispute centers on whether Apple clearly explained which features were already available and when the rest would launch. The report gives an example: Siri’s personal context understanding was promoted as launching in South Korea in early April 2025, but it actually went live in October 2026—about 18 months late. Apple responded that since Apple Intelligence gained Korean-language support last year, users have had access to dozens of features, and it recently launched Korean-language Siri AI; the company says it has cooperated with the investigation but disagrees with the conclusions and will defend itself fully. No ruling has been issued yet, and there is no penalty.

The same ads, penalized in multiple markets

This is not an isolated case. In April 2025, after an inquiry by the U.S. National Advertising Division, Apple removed the “available now” wording from its Apple Intelligence page—regulators believed it implied all features were already available and that the footnote about phased rollout was not clear enough; Apple disagreed but made the change. In May 2026, Apple paid $250 million to settle a U.S. class-action lawsuit alleging that when it launched the iPhone 16 in September 2024, it misled buyers about the availability of Apple Intelligence and Siri. The same set of ads is now being scrutinized item by item in multiple markets.
